target.title: fix(config): key agentDir collisions by volume case sensitivity
target.body:
Closes #105194

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users with case-sensitive macOS APFS or Windows NTFS volumes would hit a false `DuplicateAgentDirError` startup rejection when two agents used distinct `agentDir` paths that differed only by case, even though the filesystem treats those paths as separate directories.

## Why This Change Was Made

`canonicalizeAgentDir` no longer lowercases all darwin/win32 paths unconditionally. It probes the target volume (walking to the closest existing parent when the configured path does not exist yet) and folds case only when that volume is actually case-insensitive. Case-sensitive volumes keep case-distinct directories as distinct agent state homes, while true shared paths still collide.

## User Impact

Operators on case-sensitive volumes can configure case-distinct agent directories without a false startup collision. Common case-insensitive macOS/Windows volumes still reject case-only spelling variants that would share auth/session state.

## Evidence

Verification host: local macOS (Crabbox bypass)

Focused tests:
```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/agent-dirs.test.ts src/config/config.multi-agent-agentdir-validation.test.ts
# Test Files  2 passed (2)
# Tests  6 passed (6)
```

Path-scoped static:
```text
pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/config/agent-dirs.ts src/config/agent-dirs.test.ts  # pass
pnpm exec oxlint src/config/agent-dirs.ts src/config/agent-dirs.test.ts        # 0 warnings / 0 errors
git diff --check                                                                 # pass
```

`pnpm check:changed` ran locally: format, dependency guards, package patches, and **typecheck core** completed successfully. **typecheck core tests** was still running after ~36m with high CPU; under closeout phase budget pressure it was stopped and replaced by the path-scoped static + focused Vitest quality floor above (same risk class coverage for this two-file config surface).

Real behavior proof (case-sensitive APFS sparseimage + production `findDuplicateAgentDirs`):
```text
current_main_would_collide true
after_fix_case_distinct_dupes 0
after_fix_true_dupes 1 a,b
PROOF_OK
```

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: case-distinct `agentDir` paths on a case-sensitive volume no longer raise a false duplicate-agentDir collision, while identical paths still do.
- Environment: local macOS arm64, OpenClaw checkout at `fix/105194-agent-dir-case-sensitive-collisions` (`fd1ba84ac`), Case-sensitive APFS sparseimage mounted at `/Volumes/OC105194Proof`.
- Current-main contrast: unconditional darwin/win32 lowercasing maps `/Volumes/.../AgentState` and `/Volumes/.../agentstate` onto one collision key even when the volume stores them as distinct inodes (`current_main_would_collide true`).
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
  1. `hdiutil create -size 32m -type SPARSE -fs "Case-sensitive APFS" -volname OC105194Proof /tmp/oc-105194-proof.sparseimage && hdiutil attach …`
  2. `mkdir` case-distinct dirs on the volume
  3. `tsx` import of `findDuplicateAgentDirs` against those paths and a true shared path
  4. Focused Vitest suite for agent-dirs + multi-agent validation
- Evidence after fix: `after_fix_case_distinct_dupes 0`; `after_fix_true_dupes 1 a,b`; Vitest 6/6 pass.
- Control check: identical `agentDir` strings still report one conflict for agents `a` and `b`; only case-distinct paths on a case-sensitive volume are accepted.
- Observed result after fix: false collision gone on case-sensitive volume; true duplicates still rejected; default case-insensitive host tmp still folds case variants (covered by unit test).
- What was not tested: live Windows NTFS case-sensitive volume (same probe algorithm; not exercised on a Windows host here); full `pnpm check:changed` core-test typecheck completion (substituted as above).

## AI disclosure

This fix was authored with AI assistance (Grok). Human operator ran the auto find→fix pipeline; verification commands and Real behavior proof were executed on the local macOS host.
